title: Jain Paneer Capsicum Masala
description: A rich, tangy tomato gravy with soft paneer and sweet capsicum — no onion, garlic or root vegetables, with asafoetida and dry ginger doing the heavy lifting.
steps: Heat the ghee in a heavy pan. Add cumin seeds; when they crackle, add the asafoetida and stir for 10 seconds.
Pour in the tomato puree with the dry ginger, turmeric, chili powder and coriander. Cook on medium for 8–10 minutes until the oil separates.
Stir in the ground melon seeds and water and simmer for 3 minutes until the gravy is thick and glossy.
Add the capsicum and cook for 3 minutes so it keeps a little bite.
Fold in the paneer, crumble in the kasuri methi, add garam masala and salt, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Swirl in the cream if using, scatter cilantro and serve with steamed rice or jowar roti.

swaps.why: Gives savoury depth without any bulbs.
Fresh ginger is a root; dried ginger is accepted in most Jain kitchens.
Same creaminess, and keeps it nut-free.

tips: Many Jain households also eat before sunset — this cooks in about 35 minutes.
